Article Title: 'Feels like a dream': An Se-young completes badminton's golden sweep with Asian Games triumph over Akane Yamaguchi
Article Text:
Gold medalist South Korea's An Se-young (AP Photo)

An leaves Yamaguchi chasing shadows

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

South Korea's An Se-young gestures after her win against Japan's Akane Yamaguchi. (AP Photo)

From controversy to another major title

An Se-young added another glittering chapter to her extraordinary career on Tuesday, defeating Japan’s three-time world champion Akane Yamaguchi 21-17, 21-9 to win Asian Games gold and underline her status as the world’s No. 1-ranked female badminton player.The South Korean star has now collected virtually every major prize the sport has to offer. Already a Paris Olympic champion and two-time world champion, An has added a second Asian Games gold medal to her collection, further strengthening her extraordinary claim to the top of the women’s game.An dropped to her knees after sealing victory, before arching backwards and looking skyward in an emotional celebration.“It feels like a dream,” An said. “I am so happy and I'm overwhelmed with emotion as I think back to all the hard work I've put in.”The final was a demonstration of An’s athleticism, court coverage and relentless pressure. She repeatedly used the full width and depth of the court, forcing Yamaguchi into long, exhausting movements before finding openings to finish points.“I decided to approach the match with the aim of making my opponent feel rushed and forcing her to move around a lot,” An said.Yamaguchi, a three-time world champion, struggled to match An’s pace in the second game as the South Korean surged away to a commanding 21-9 victory.An had earlier defeated China’s Chen Yufei in the semifinals, extending her winning streak against her Chinese rival to five matches.An’s journey to the top has also included difficult moments. After winning Olympic gold in Paris, she criticised South Korea’s national training system, saying she had been forced to play through a knee injury and questioning some training methods. She later backed away from her threat to pursue an independent path.But on the court, An’s response has been emphatic. With another Asian Games title secured, the 24-year-old has once again demonstrated why she sits at the summit of women’s badminton.
Article Summary: An Se-young defeated Japan’s three-time world champion Akane Yamaguchi 21-17, 21-9 to win Asian Games gold. The South Korean star has now collected virtually every major prize the sport has to offer.

Jaipur: The race for the Rajasthan Cricket Association (RCA) presidency reached a dramatic crescendo following the withdrawal of nominations on Monday, with the candidate field narrowing down to a high-stakes showdown between Dhananjai Singh Khimsar and Brij Kishore Upadhyay.Electoral officer AK Pande confirmed that 18 nominations were withdrawn out of the 30 initially received, leaving 12 candidates in the fray for six executive posts. With exactly two contenders remaining per seat, straight head-to-head battles have been drawn across the board.RCA insiders suggest the odds currently favour Jodhpur District Cricket Association (DCA) president Khimsar, whose ‘resilience’ and ‘institutional knowledge’ have kept him at the centre of state cricket affairs for years.He was on the verge of claiming the presidency in 2024 before the process was disrupted, and he has maintained a consistent presence on every ad-hoc committee formed to manage RCA operations between 2024 and 2026.However, the opposition is far from subdued. “Upadhyay's (Dausa DCA secretary) entry into the race has injected fresh drama, particularly when he arrived to file his nomination papers accompanied by veteran leader and finance commission chairman Arun Chaturvedi, a prominent figure close to the chief minister, which political insiders suggest indicates govt backing.That said, Khimsar also possesses immense political weight, being the son of the state’s health minister Gajendra Singh Khimsar. Also, let’s not forget that Dhananjai’s extended family shares a strong connection with an influential Central minister,” a source said.Party insiders pointed towards how these elections also bring to light deeper internal factions within the BJP. Earlier, three distinct groups within the party ecosystem were fighting the polls. Following Parakram Singh Rathore’s exit, the contest has condensed into a ‘direct battle between the two remaining camps’.The dynamics of the presidential race have altered now. “Parakram withdrew due to a lack of political support, as he was reportedly running solely on the legacy of his father, former Leader of Opposition Rajendra Singh Rathore, rather than building a broader consensus. And district cricket associations like Bharatpur, Dholpur and Dausa also kept him under the impression that they were in his support, but in reality they were not,” added another source.The competitive spirit extends across the entire ballot, with straight contests shaping up for all executive positions. Mohit Yadav will face Ratan Singh Shekhawat for the vice-president's role, while also squaring off against Pinkesh Kumar Jain for the secretary's position. Administrative continuity defines the joint secretary race, where Vinod Saharan will compete against Rajesh Saraswat, and Ashish Tiwari and Vishnu Prakash Agarwal will battle for the treasurer's post.The executive member contest will be decided between Aristh Singhvi and Dharamveer Singh Shekhawat.
Article Summary: Dhananjai Singh Khimsar and Brij Kishore Upadhyay locked in presidential battle. 18 nominations were withdrawn out of the 30 initially received, leaving 12 candidates in the fray for six executive posts. Straight head-to-head battles have been drawn across the board.

Article Title: After four decades, top-tier cricket returns to Srinagar with Irani Cup showdown
Article Text:
Srinagar’s Sher-i-Kashmir Stadium

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What aspect of the Irani Trophy match are you most looking forward to? Historic significance High-profile cricket in Srinagar The venue improvements 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

For four decades, the story of top-tier cricket at the Sher-i-Kashmir Stadium lived in archivist notes and yellowed newspaper clippings. The venue’s international history is brief but historic. On October 13 1983, it hosted its first One Day International between India and the West Indies, a game infamous for pitch disruptions during the lunch interval, followed by rain and dust storms where Desmond Haynes’s unbeaten 55 sealed a revised victory for the visitors.Three years later, on September 9, 1986, Allan Border’s match-winning 90 not out eclipsed Sunil Gavaskar’s 52 off 56 balls as Australia edged India by three wickets.While an Irani Cup fixture in Srinagar may not carry the international label of those 1980s ODIs, hosting domestic cricket’s premier red-ball tournament marks the most significant high-profile showcase the state has seen in generations. The occasion is made sweeter by the team’s meteoric rise as Jammu and Kashmir, created history last season by winning their maiden Ranji Trophy title after a 67-year wait, defeating powerhouse Karnataka in the final.​Sensing excitement around the five-day match, the J&K Cricket Association (JKCA) is working around the clock to ensure the venue is fully upgraded.​Speaking about the extensive preparations underway, head of cricket operations Majid Dar told TOI, "Basically, this ground was not meant for live matches, but the BCCI had already sent a team for a recce in advance, one-and-a-half months back. They gave us a checklist of certain requirements like broadcasting rooms, camera towers, and a few other things. We were able to fulfill those requirements on time, and we are ready to host the match. "​Reflecting on the historical milestone, Dar added, "This is history. Such a big event is taking place after three to four decades. It is a massive boost for cricket lovers and cricketers of the Valley. We are very excited to host the Irani Trophy for the first time," he said.​To handle the expected surge of spectators, seating arrangements have been installed around the perimeter. "Currently, the seating capacity of the ground was around 2000 to 2500. We have increased it now, making it a total seating arrangement for 5000 people," Dar explained. "We do not want the venue to get overcrowded; we want to keep the situation controlled. Everyone who enters the ground should have the tickets for the match as there will be tight security in place.Entry to the ground will be strictly regulated, with tickets issued free of cost to fans on a first-come, first-served basis. "We will distribute passes for the general public on a first-come, first-served basis, while some seats are allocated for invitees and personal guests. Passes will be issued on Sept 30 from 1:00pm to 4:00pm at the stadium premises upon verification of an Aadhaar card or one more valid ID proof," Dar added.​Beyond temporary spectator facilities, the JKCA has built lasting infrastructure to support high-profile broadcasts. "The broadcasting room was not there earlier, so we created a broadcasting room in a short span of time. These structures are not makeshift, they are built to stay as we have two live games scheduled. We have also set up dedicated rooms for match officials, renovated the dressing rooms, and erected TV towers required for the live broadcast," Dar said.
Article Summary: Sher-i-Kashmir Stadium in Srinagar will host the Irani Trophy match. The ground hosted its first One Day International on October 13 1983. The J&K Cricket Association is working around the clock to ensure the venue is fully upgraded.

Article Title: ‘The Indian bowlers are incredibly accurate’: Peter Handscomb on the challenge of facing India
Article Text:

Chennai: There was a time when Peter Handscomb felt Test cricket had exposed the limitations of his game. The 35-year-old batter is back in India with a technique and mindset shaped by years of adjustment.Handscomb, who is leading the Australia ‘A’ side, did not have the ideal start in the first unofficial Test against India ‘A’ in Puducherry. But for the veteran batter, the tour is as much about the present as it is about keeping an eye on the future.Handscomb has played 11 Tests against India and believes the key is not simply to attack but to identify scoring opportunities against accurate bowling.“You’ve got to attack when you get the opportunity to score, but it is tough,” Handscomb told TOI ahead of the second ‘Test’ that starts on Tuesday. “The Indian bowlers are incredibly accurate, consistent and don’t give a lot of bad balls. You’ve got to try and find a way to score off good balls. It can be tough when the ball misbehaves, but that’s the challenge of playing in India.”More than half of his Test matches have come against India.“It’s tough to keep coming up against India, but it’s also such an amazing thing to do,” he said. “There are some of the best players in the world here and I’m lucky enough to have played against some of them.”

Article Title: PT Usha’s 42-year reign ends: How Vithya Ramraj finally broke India’s 400m hurdles mark
Article Text:
Vithya Ramraj

"I knew she would peak in this competition. I was almost sure that she would do sub 54.5, but it was 54.7. But it is okay because, without progression, you cannot perform at that big level. Atthe Delhi meet on Sep 10,she fell down from a hurdle;otherwise, we were expecting around 55s there and then the progression from there (to the National record).” —Nehpal Singh | VITHYA’S COACH

Still way behind

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bengaluru: For more than four decades, PT Usha ’s 55.42 seconds remained the gold standard for India’s women’s 400m hurdlers. Very few athletes matched her class, and even fewer had the grit to put in the hard yards and challenge the magical number, while many others simply found it insurmountable.Even as the new millennium dawned, India’s top women hurdlers struggled to dip below the one-minute mark. That time was clocked at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics, when Usha lost the bronze by milliseconds.It was an achievement that put her on the same pedestal as ‘Flying Sikh’ Milkha Singh, who also came close to a bronze in the men’s 400m at the 1960 Rome Olympics.As India enters the cycle for the 2028 Los Angeles Games, the national mark which became nearly permanent has been erased. Fittingly, the ‘Payyoli Express’ has been overtaken by the Coimbatore Super Fast. Vithya Ramraj had earlier equalled the mark three years ago in the heats at the Hangzhou Asiad.When asked why it took so long for Usha’s record to be erased, experts agreed that Usha had set the bar very high, very early in a highly demanding event.“The time clocked in 1984 was world class. PT Usha was a generational talent and she had the talent to go even faster.Then we hardly had athletes of that calibre,” said noted coach PB Jaikumar.Jaikumar trained Anu Raghavan for many years, leading to her winning the bronze at the 2010 Asiad. The 33-year-old, returning to the Asiad after a 14-year gap, clocked her personal best time of 55.88s in Nagoya and finished a creditable fifth on Monday.“It’s a highly technical event, where you need both speed and the technique to fly over the 10 hurdles. We have produced very few athletes of Usha’s calibre over the decades, which is why the record stood for so long,” added Jaikumar.Experts also felt that the athletics federation’s focus on making a quality 4x400m relay squad was another reason for the record to stay for so long.“We had quite a few top-class 400m runners but very few of them did well in the individual events like the 400m or 400m hurdles. The moment they began to impress, coaches eyed including them in the relay squad and over the years, priorities shifted from individual events to the relay,” another national coach said.Jaikumar also said India still has a long way to catch up with the current world standards despite lowering the record below 55 seconds.“It’s a big feat to break a 42-year-old record but you can’t read too much into it. The new record will still place Vithya among the 35-40 fastest in the world. That shows how far we have to catch up. The main takeaway should be the confidence for our athletes that all records can be broken, provided they keep working hard.“We know our athletes don’t stand much of a chance in the Olympics, so we should target the Asian Games. We should train in such a way that our athletes achieve their personal best at these Games. Count how many of our athletes achieved their personal bests at these Games. Count how many of our athletes achieved their personal bests in Nagoya,” Jaikumar signed off.
Article Summary: Vithya Ramraj clocked her personal best time of 55.88s in Nagoya. The 33-year- old had earlier equalled the mark three years ago in the heats at the Hangzhou Asiad. The time was clocked at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics, when Usha lost the bronze.

Article Title: Murali Sreeshankar twists ankle, refuses wheelchair and returns to win Asian Games silver
Article Text:
India's Murali Sreeshankar (PTI Photo)

Podium in javelin

Double silver for Gulveer

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Parul makes it two in two days

Nagoya: The image of Indian long jump ace Murali Sreeshankar twisting his ankle on his fourth jump on a rain-swept Monday night at the Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium will be a tough one to forget.As the 27-year-old landed awkwardly on his right leg and writhed in pain, memories of the ruptured left patellar tendon that ruled him out of the Paris Olympics and kept him out of the sandpit for almost two years came flooding back. He limped out with the help of medical staff and was offered a wheelchair, which he refused. Even when the medical team advised him not to return, he shrugged them off.He did not need to take his next two attempts. He had already breached the eight-metre mark with his second jump of 8.07m, enough to fetch him silver and a repeat of his podium finish from the previous edition. China’s Yuhao Shi, with a season’s best of 8.17m, took gold. The other Indian in the field, Solomon Patturaj (7.70m), finished seventh.Once his medal was confirmed, Sreeshankar, who won silver at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games, limped over to collect the Indian flag, wrapped himself in the tricolour and celebrated briefly before heading off for treatment.It was a productive day for India in athletics, with the team picking up three silver and three bronze medals.The javelin competition was without Neeraj Chopra, but India did not miss out on a podium finish. In fact, there were two.Yashvir Singh saved his best for last, clinching silver with a season’s best of 85.72m. Fancied Sri Lankan Rumesh Pathirage, in red-hot form, continued his rich vein of form to take gold with 88.55m, while Rohit Yadav completed the podium with 84.35m.Olympic champion Arshad Nadeem from Pakistan, who is going through a lean patch, managed an underwhelming 80.29m, which was incidentally his season’s best.Pathirage, who has breached the 90m mark three times this year, took some time to find his rhythm in the testing conditions, allowing Yashvir to take the lead. But with his fourth attempt of 88.33m, the 23-year-old Sri Lankan moved ahead and only got better from there.Gulveer Singh, who won silver in the 10,000m three days ago, returned to claim another silver in the 1500m with a personal best of 3:36.72.Gulveer never fell behind in the race and briefly took the lead at the 200m bend, but Japan’s Kazuto Iizawa produced a late burst in the home stretch to take gold in a Games record 3:36.35.Gulveer later admitted he had not paced the race well enough.“I wanted to do better, but I’m glad I could win a medal. I was pacing according to the long-distance running, but he (Iizawa) took off and I couldn’t keep pace,” said the 28-year-old.Parul Chaudhary, who took silver in the 3000m steeplechase on Saturday, delivered another strong performance to settle for bronze in the 5000m.Parul looked set for silver but could not produce the final push and clocked 15:14.61.The day’s biggest disappointment came in the men’s 3000m steeplechase, where defending champion Avinash Sable finished fourth in 8:21.67. Sable, returning from injury and having said he was peaking for the Games, looked off the pace for much of the race.There was also heartbreak for the women’s 4x100m relay team, which finished fourth despite clocking a season’s best. The quartet of Abinaya Rajarajan, Sneha Sathyanarayana, Sudeshna Shivankar and Tamanna timed 43.57 seconds.
Article Summary: Long jump ace Murali Sreeshankar twisted his ankle on his fourth jump. The 27-year-old landed awkwardly on his right leg and writhed in pain. He limped out with the help of medical staff and was offered a wheelchair. China’s Yuhao Shi took gold.

Article Title: Neeru Dhanda leads India to women’s trap team silver at Asian Games
Article Text:
India’s Neeru Dhanda celebrates after helping the women’s trap team win silver at the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya. Dhanda also qualified for the individual final after finishing joint-second in qualification with a score of 118/125.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Neeru Dhanda produced a composed and consistent display on the range to lead India to a silver medal in the women’s trap team event at the Asian Games here on Tuesday.Neeru, Aashima Ahlawat and Manisha Keer combined for 328 points to finish second behind China, which won gold with 346. Kuwait took bronze with 325.The medal was built around a strong individual showing from Neeru, who finished the qualification round with 118 hits out of 125. She was joint-first in the individual standings and also qualified for the individual final.Neeru began with 24 hits in the opening round and followed it with a perfect 24 in the second round. She added 24 in the third, 23 in the fourth and 23 in the fifth to finish on 118. Only Qatar's Ray Bassil, also on 118, was ahead on the ranking tiebreak.Aashima finished with 106, while Manisha contributed 104 as the Indian trio accumulated 328 points. Aashima's scores across the five rounds were 20, 22, 23, 19 and 22, while Manisha shot 19, 21, 22, 22 and 20.China's gold-medal winning trio finished on 346, with their five-round totals reading 65, 71, 70, 72 and 68. Kuwait completed the podium with 325.For India, the silver adds another medal to its shooting campaign at the Aichi-Nagoya Games. It is also India's second Asian Games medal in the women's trap team event, after the silver won at Hangzhou in 2023 by Manisha Keer, Rajeshwari Kumari and Preeti Rajak.The medal also takes India's shooting haul at the 2026 Asian Games to 13 medals, while India's overall tally moves to 46 medals.But the immediate focus will now turn to Neeru. Having already put together one of the strongest qualification performances in the field, she will return for the individual final with an opportunity to add another medal to India's tally.
Article Summary: Neeru, Aashima Ahlawat and Manisha Keer combined for 328 points to finish second behind China, which won gold with 346. Dhanda also qualified for the individual final after finishing joint-second in qualification with a score of 118/125.

Article Title: Shapath Bharadwaj survives tense shoot-off to reach trap shooting final at Asian Games
Article Text:
India's Shapath Bharadwaj (PTI Photo)

India add another shooting medal

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India’s Shapath Bharadwaj booked his place in the men’s individual trap shooting final after surviving a tense three-way shoot-off at the Asian Games on Tuesday.Shapath finished joint-seventh in qualification with 117 points, forcing him into a shoot-off against Qatar’s Mohammed Al-Rumaihi and Kazakhstan’s Alisher Aisalbayev for the two remaining places in the final.The Indian held his nerve in the decider, edging Al-Rumaihi to seal his place in the medal round.Kynan Chenai, who won bronze at Hangzhou 2023, finished 16th with 115 points, while Ahvar Rizvi ended 32nd with 107. Both missed out on qualification for the individual final.The result gave Shapath a chance to fight for a medal, although India’s men’s trap team could not make the podium.Shapath, Kynan and Ahvar combined for 339 points to finish sixth in the team event.Earlier, India’s women’s trap team of Neeru Dhanda, Aashima Ahlawat and Manisha Keer secured silver, taking the country’s shooting medal tally to 13.The Indian trio accumulated 328 points after three days of the 125-shot qualification round to finish second and hold off Kuwait’s challenge.China won the gold medal with an aggregate of 346, while Kuwait took bronze with 325.Neeru also progressed to the women’s individual final after finishing joint-top in qualification with 118 points.Aashima and Manisha, however, could not make the final. Aashima scored 106 to finish 16th, while Manisha registered 104 and ended 23rd.India’s 13 shooting medals include just one gold so far. Kamaljeet and Suruchi Singh claimed that title in the mixed 10m air pistol event with a stellar performance.Overall, India’s medal tally at the ongoing Asian Games stands at 46, comprising four gold, 21 silver and 21 bronze medals.
Article Summary: Shapath Bharadwaj booked his place in the men’s individual trap shooting final after surviving a tense three-way shoot-off at the Asian Games on Tuesday. India's women's trap team of Neeru Dhanda, Aashima Ahlawat and Manisha Keer secured silver, taking the country's shooting medal tally to 13.

Article Title: Asian Games: Ankush Panghal rallies from behind to stun Uzbek world champion and reach gold-medal bout
Article Text:
Ankush Panghal (IANS Photo)

Ankush turns the tide after losing opening round

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Parveen Hooda also enters final

NEW DELHI: India’s Ankush Panghal produced a stirring comeback to stun reigning world champion Fazliddin Erkinboev of Uzbekistan and storm into the men’s 80kg gold-medal bout at the Asian Games on Tuesday.Ankush was up against it after dropping the opening round. But the Indian boxer fought back in the second. He then turned the semifinal on its head with a commanding final round, sweeping all five judges’ cards to seal the 4-1 victory.The win sends Ankush into the final and gives India another chance to add to its boxing medal tally. His performance was built on a strong finish after a difficult start, as he stayed in the contest and raised his intensity when the bout was on the line.The semifinal began with Fazliddin taking control, earning a 4-1 verdict in the first round. Ankush needed a response to keep his gold-medal hopes alive, and delivered one in the second, which he won 3-2 on the judges’ cards.With the contest finely balanced heading into the third, Ankush produced his best boxing of the bout. He dominated the final round and secured a unanimous 5-0 verdict, completing the comeback against the reigning world champion.Earlier, India’s Parveen Hooda advanced to the women’s 65kg gold-medal bout after defeating China’s Li Shu 5-0 in her semifinal.Parveen’s progress marks an improvement on her bronze-medal finish at the previous Asian Games in Hangzhou. That medal was later taken away after the International Testing Agency suspended her for 22 months over a whereabouts failure.Indian boxers have already surpassed their four-medal haul from the previous edition, with six pugilists having secured entries into medal rounds at these Games. Narender Berwal, the bronze medallist from Hangzhou in the men’s +90kg category, was also scheduled to fight later on Tuesday for a place in the final.
Article Summary: Ankush Panghal stuns world champion Fazliddin Erkinboev of Uzbekistan. Indian boxer turns the tide after losing opening round of 80kg bout. Parveen Hooda also enters final of women's 65kg gold-medal bout.

Article Title: Delhi Capitals cricketer back in squad ahead of Ranji Trophy days after bail in sexual offence case
Article Text:
Delhi Capitals' Abhishek Porel

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bengal squad:

Abishek Porel has been included in Bengal’s senior men’s squad for practice matches against Assam at the ACA Stadium in Guwahati, marking his return to the state side after his arrest in a case involving allegations of rape and other sexual offences.The Cricket Association of Bengal (CAB) announced the squad on Tuesday, with Sudip Chatterjee named captain. The Bengal team is scheduled to leave Kolkata on September 30 and return on October 6 as preparations begin for the 2026 Ranji Trophy season.Porel, who plays for Delhi Capitals in the Indian Premier League, has not featured in competitive cricket since IPL 2026, where he played four matches.The wicketkeeper-batter was arrested by Kolkata Police on August 11 following a complaint filed by a young medical student. The FIR was registered at Magra Police Station on June 30.The complainant alleged that Porel had sexual relations with her on the promise of marriage. She also accused him of threatening to make intimate photographs of her public and alleged that she was forced into a physical relationship.Porel denied the allegations before his arrest.The cricketer was booked under 19 sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, with most of the charges being non-bailable.Sections of the Information Technology Act were also included in the case.Porel spent more than a month in jail before being granted bail on September 18 in cases including rape and having sexual relations on the promise of marriage.The legal proceedings had come before the Calcutta High Court on August 11, when Magra Police informed Justice Sougat Bhattacharyya about Porel’s arrest. He was subsequently produced before the Chinsurah court, where the judge directed the police to examine electronic devices in his possession.Police later arrested another friend of Porel as well as the woman complainant in connection with the case.Porel’s selection in the Bengal squad comes just over a week after he was granted bail and puts him back in the state setup ahead of the new domestic season.Sudip Chatterjee (Captain), Abhimanyu Easwaran, Ankur Paul, Ankit Shukla, Sumanta Gupta, Subham Chatterjee, Abishek Porel (W.K.), Shakir Habib Gandhi (W.K.), Pradipta Pramanik, Karan Lal, Aamir Gani, Soummyadip Mandal, Suraj Sindhu Jaiswal, Md. Kaif, Geet Puri, and Ishan Porel.
Article Summary: Abishek Porel included in Bengal's senior men's squad for practice matches against Assam. Wicketkeeper-batter was arrested by Kolkata Police on August 11 following a complaint filed by a young medical student. Delhi Capitals star was granted bail on September 18.

Article Title: Back from hamstring injury, Ayush Mhatre to play his first competitive match in 5 months
Article Text:
Ayush Mhatre (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI:In a major boost to Mumbai ahead of the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season, opener Ayush Mhatre, out of action since he suffered a bad hamstring injury while playing for the Chennai Super Kings during IPL-2026, will play his first competitive match in almost five months when he will turn out in a Kanga League 'B' Division match for his club Sainath CC on Friday.On Tuesday, Mhatre and senior middle-order batter Siddhesh Lad, who will be Mumbai's captain for the 2026-27 domestic season, underwent match simulation exercises at the Cricket Club of India. Lad had dislocated his shoulder during the T20 Mumbai League final in June. "Both Lad and Mhatre have been asked to undergo match simulation exercise and play the final round of the Kanga League on Friday. They will be given RTP (Return to Play) by the MCA's physio only after they come through this successfully," a source in the Mumbai Cricket Association told TOI."Ayush is now completely fit and has recovered from his injuries in both the hamstrings. He has been training at the Mumbai Cricket Association's indoor facility at BKC for the past 10 days, and is training at Sainath Cricket Club today. He is undergoing a two-day match simulation, organised by the Mumbai Cricket Association for Mumbai's Ranji Trophy probables, at the Brabourne Stadium from today. He will turn out for Sainath Cricket Club in a Kanga League 'B Division game on Friday," Ayush's father Yogesh Mhatre told TOI on Monday.Mhatre had been ruled out of IPL-2026 due to a left hamstring injury. The 19-year-old suffered the injury while batting during CSK's game against Sunrisers Hyderabad on April 18."Ayush's injury will require a rehabilitation period of 6-12 weeks. We wish Ayush a speedy recovery," CSK had posted on social media."It looks pretty bad, unfortunately. And he's going to be a big, big loss because he's been in really nice touch for us," Mike Hussey, the CSK batting coach had said about Mhatre's hamstring injury.Mhatre scored 201 runs in six innings at a strike rate of 177.87 in IPL-2026, before the injury forced him to sit on the sidelines.

In the five-over rain-truncated contest India managed 32/4 and then scrapped through with a two-run margin.“We can’t take any team in the Asian Games lightly because the wicket here cannot be set to a particular standard. Article Text:

Fastest centuries Boundary percentage Consistency despite aggression Performance in powerplays 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

The 30-ball ton was, oddly, the least surprising part of what Abhishek Sharma did at the Arun Jaitley Stadium. It isn't even his fastest hundred. What's odd about the innings is what it says about the number sitting next to that extraordinary strike rate: his average.Somewhere in Abhishek Sharma's memory, though, there's a faster century still. It came two years ago, for Punjab against Meghalaya in a Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy fixture nobody outside domestic cricket was watching: 28 balls, no fanfare.So when he reached three figures in 30 deliveries against Afghanistan in New Delhi, becoming the fastest T20I centurion ever produced by a Full Member nation and only the third-fastest in the format's history overall, it wasn't a discovery. It was a confirmation, delivered on a bigger stage, of something the data had already been saying for a while.The ground has some history with him already. Eight years earlier, on the same square when it was still called Feroz Shah Kotla, a 17-year-old Sharma walked out at number six for Delhi Daredevils against Royal Challengers Bangalore and top-scored on IPL debut — an unbeaten 46 off 19 balls. It was the innings that first put his name into circulation.None of that is really the story, though. The story is what his average has been doing while all this has been going on.After 58 T20I innings, Abhishek averages 33.18 at a strike rate of 194.55. Among those who have batted at least 20 times in T20Is since Abhishek's debut in July 2024, nobody has struck as quickly as his 194.55 per 100 balls.Put that alongside the numbers of his closest opening peers and the combination starts to look strange. Phil Salt, across almost the same number of innings, averages 34.34 at 165.89: a fraction higher on average, nearly thirty runs per hundred balls slower. Finn Allen's numbers read 28.67 and 170.74; Travis Head's, 28.40 and 156.69. Multiply strike rate by average and divide by 100 and you get a rough figure for scoring speed without giving up the average: Abhishek comes out at 64.56, against 56.97 for Salt, 48.95 for Allen and 44.50 for Head.The gap isn't really about six-hitting or bravado. It's that T20 cricket generally punishes extreme aggression with a lower average, and in Abhishek's case, over more than fifty innings now, it hasn't.Look closer and the shape of his batting explains some of it. Of his 1,858 T20I runs, 1,484 (79.9%) have come in boundaries. In the Afghanistan innings that figure spiked to 94.44%, the highest boundary share recorded in any men's T20I century.He hits a six in T20Is every 7.58 balls, comfortably ahead of Allen (8.47), Salt (12.47) and Head (14.20). Zoom out to his whole T20 career, across formats, and he reached his hundredth six faster, by balls faced, than anyone the format has seen, edging West Indies' Evin Lewis. Among Indian batters with 50 or more T20 sixes, nobody has matched his rate of clearing the boundary. He's the best of the lot, streets ahead of Sanju Samson, Shivam Dube, Suryakumar Yadav and Yuvraj Singh , the mentor whose fastest-fifty record he's now threatened on at least three occasions.The clearest expression of the method is the powerplay. His strike rate in an innings' first ten balls, 176, is the joint-highest on record, level with Tim David: he isn't feeling out the pitch before he attacks. His boundary percentage inside the powerplay, 33.48% according to CricViz, is the best among batters with 500-plus T20I runs.This has happened before, too. India have breached 90 in a T20I powerplay four times, and Abhishek has been the one doing the damage on every occasion: 59 not out off 21 against England at the Wankhede last year, 51 not out off 14 against New Zealand in Guwahati this year, 51 off 19 in the World Cup final in Ahmedabad, where he reached fifty in 18 balls under the most pressure he's likely ever faced. His 76 not out off 22 balls is simply the largest number yet on that list. His opening stand with Samson, 142 off 59 balls, is now the fastest century opening partnership for India in T20Is by run rate, overtaking a stand between KL Rahul and Rohit Sharma from Indore in 2017.None of this comes free. Abhishek walked into this year's T20 World Cup and made three consecutive ducks, followed that with 15, 10 and 9, and salvaged the campaign with two match-defining fifties, one in a must-win Super Eight game against Zimbabwe, the other in the final. Eight innings, 141 runs, an average of 17.62. "As a batter, as a cricketer, sometimes [my form is] going to go up and down," he said afterwards, and there's little sense he sees the ducks as a separate problem from the sixes. They're the same bet, landing differently.And 2026 has underlined that cost. Abhishek has been dismissed for a duck 10 times in T20 cricket this calendar year, the most by any batter in a year, ahead of Rashid Khan's nine in 2019 and Shadab Khan's nine in 2024. Five of those have come off the first ball, making him the joint-most prolific first-ball duck-maker in a calendar year in T20Is, alongside Rwanda's Kevin Irakoze in 2023 and Richard Ngarava in 2024.What's changed isn't the risk-taking. It's how deliberately he manages it. Against the Rashid Khan, Mohammad Nabi and Mujeeb Ur Rahman spin trio in the Afghanistan series, he made a conscious tactical switch, going only forward or down the pitch, never back, and scored 54 off 15 against them, including 4, 4, 6 off three straight Rashid deliveries in the last over of the powerplay.In the first two games, camped on the back foot against the same bowlers, he'd managed only 29 off 17. "It's always about me backing my shots because I don't have a lot of shots," he said earlier this year, after an 85 off 34 against New Zealand, which sounds like modesty until you notice how precisely that limited toolkit is being aimed.This is now his tenth century in all forms of T20 cricket, level with Virat Kohli for the most by an Indian batter, and his third T20I hundred, level with Samson, and behind only Rohit Sharma and Suryakumar Yadav in India's own list. The number worth sitting with isn't the 30 balls. It's how Abhishek has managed to keep his average above 30 while scoring at a strike rate of nearly 195.
Article Summary: Abhishek Sharma is the fastest T20I centurion ever produced by a Full Member nation. He averages 33.18 at a strike rate of 194.55 per 100 balls. He hits a six in T20Is every 7.58 balls, comfortably ahead of Finn Allen (8.47) and Travis Head (12.20) His strike rate in an innings' first ten balls is the joint-highest on the pitch.

Article Title: ‘She can go sub-54’: After breaking PT Usha’s 42-year-old record, Vithya Ramraj’s coach sets new target
Article Text:
Vithya Ramraj with her coach Nehpal Singh

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nehpal Singh is basking in the glory as the coach of Vithya Ramraj who bettered PT Usha's 42-year-old record, three years after equalling that elusive record in the women's 400m hurdles at the last Asian Games in Hangzhou.Asked about the five-year plan, which took Indian athletics to a new high with his ward dipping under the 55-second and lowering the new mark to 54.75 seconds, the coach from Rajasthan, whose family is settled in Salem for the last 20 years, said: "Vithya would have set the record last year itself but for the injury at the Asian championships. She sustained a serious ankle injury but ran with the swollen ankles at the Asian meet and still won the bronze.This year I was waiting eagerly for everything to go right and today she did it. ""I knew she would peak in this competition. I was almost sure that she would do sub 54.5, but it was 54.7. But it is okay because, without progression, you cannot perform at that big level. At the Delhi meet on Sep 10, she fell down from a hurdle; otherwise, we were expecting around 55.0s there and then the progression from there (to the National record)," the former national-level sprinter turned coach Nehpal told TOI from Nagoya.Asked about the sacrifices made by the 28-year-old from Coimbatore, he said: "She is very dedicated. Both of us have not gone home all year as we were training fully focussed on the big meet."Nehpal, who started coaching her in 2021 and holds a World Athletics coaching certification, lauded Vithya for her dedication. "Vithya is the most consistent athlete. She has been in the top 3 in India in the 400m for the last five years. And for the last five years, she's been No. 1 in the 400m hurdles.""The day she asked me, 'I want to join you for training,'... I was like, yes, we can do. Okay. We can do this national record. Once the national record was equaled, I realized she could do much more. My plan was sub 55. And this year, we figured out that no, we can go sub 54," said Nehpal who also trains Vithya's twin sister Nithya. Nithya, who is recovering from an injury, had finished seventh in the 100m hurdles at the last Asiad.Moving forward, the coach and Vithya have set their sights on the World Championships and the LA Games."The qualification mark for the World Championships and Olympics is 54.0s. Otherwise, she'll make the Games easily by her ranking," he added without going into the details of the next five-year plan.
Article Summary: Vithya Ramraj bettered PT Usha's 42-year-old record in the women's 400m hurdles. Vithya would have set the record last year itself but for the injury at the Asian championships. Nehpal Singh, who started coaching her in 2021 and holds a World Athletics coaching certification, lauded her dedication.

Article Title: Asian Games: Narender Berwal wins bronze in heavyweight boxing as Parveen Hooda, Ankush Panghal reach finals
Article Text:
Narender Berwal

Narender unable to trouble reigning world champion

Parveen, Ankush storm into gold-medal bouts

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India’s Narender Berwal secured a bronze medal in the men’s +90kg boxing event at the Asian Games after losing his semifinal bout to Kazakhstan’s reigning world champion Aibek Oralbay on Tuesday.Narender struggled to match Oralbay’s pace and power in a one-sided contest, going down 0-5 on the judges’ scorecards. The Indian boxer lost all three rounds by unanimous decision and missed out on a place in the gold-medal bout.Despite Narender’s defeat, it was a productive day for Indian boxing, with Parveen Hooda and Ankush Panghal winning their respective semifinals to advance to the finals. The pair’s victories helped India surpass its four-medal haul from the previous edition, with six Indian boxers now assured of medals at Aichi-Nagoya Games.Oralbay took charge from the opening bell, winning the first round 5-0 to put Narender under immediate pressure. The Indian needed a strong response in the second round, but the Kazakh boxer continued to dominate and secured another 5-0 verdict on the judges’ cards.Narender was unable to mount a turnaround in the final round, which Oralbay also won 5-0. The semifinal loss ended the Indian’s run at the Games, but he leaves with a bronze medal after reaching the last four in the heavyweight category.Earlier, Parveen defeated China’s Li Shu 5-0 in the women’s 65kg semifinal to book her place in the final. The win marks an improvement on her bronze-medal finish at Hangzhou, a result that was later annulled after the International Testing Agency suspended her for 22 months over a whereabouts failure.Parveen has also become only the third Indian woman boxer to reach an Asian Games final, following MC Mary Kom, who won gold in 2014, and Lovlina Borgohain , who claimed silver at the previous edition.Ankush then produced a stirring comeback in the men’s 80kg semifinal, rallying from behind to beat Uzbekistan’s reigning world champion Fazliddin Erkinboev. After losing the opening round 4-1, Ankush took the second 3-2 before sweeping the final round 5-0 to seal his place in the gold-medal bout.Narender’s bronze and the two semifinal wins added to India’s boxing medal count, with six pugilists having secured medal-round places at the Games.
Article Summary: Narender Berwal loses to Aibek Oralbay in men's +90kg semifinal. Indian boxer loses all three rounds by unanimous decision. Parveen Hooda and Ankush Panghal advance to women's 65kg final. India now has six boxing medals at Asian Games.

Article Title: Neeru Dhanda scripts history with India’s first individual Asian Games gold in women’s trap
Article Text:

Neeru Dhanda scripted history on Tuesday by becoming the first Indian shooter to win an Asian Games gold medal in the women’s trap individual event, smashing the continental record in the process.The 26-year-old from Haryana produced a score of 28 in the eight-shooter final to surpass the previous Asian record of 24 and claim the gold medal.Neeru’s triumph came after she had helped India secure silver in the women’s trap team event earlier in the competition. Her latest achievement is even more significant as no Indian woman trap or skeet shooter had previously won an individual medal at the Asian Games.Randhir Singh had won India’s historic individual gold in the men’s individual trap event at the 1978 Games, while Ronjan Sodhi claimed the men’s double trap individual gold at the 2010 edition.Neeru had entered the final as one of the joint leaders after topping qualification alongside Qatar’s Ray Bassil with 118 points. The score was also a Games record for qualification.The Haryana shooter has been in exceptional form this year. In July, she became the first Indian woman to win a World Cup gold medal in the trap event at the Shotgun World Cup in Italy.Earlier in the Asian Games, Neeru, Aashima Ahlawat and Manisha Keer combined for 328 to win silver in the women’s trap team event.China took gold with 346, while Kuwait secured bronze with 325.The Chinese team comprised Liu Shanshan, Sun Yunong and Zhu Jingyu, while Kuwait were represented by Alhawal Shahad, Abdulmalik Hajar and Alhawal Sarah.Aashima and Manisha could not make the individual final, finishing 16th and 23rd respectively in qualification after scoring 106 and 104.
Article Summary: Neeru Dhanda becomes first Indian shooter to win an Asian Games gold medal. Article Title: ‘It’s his bad luck’: Rumesh Pathirage reveals he missed Neeraj Chopra after Asian Games gold
Article Text:
Neeraj Chopra and Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage

Pathirage and Chopra's changing fortunes

'Yashvir and Rohit are very good'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

World Championships and LA Olympics next

Sri Lankan javelin thrower Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage said he missed seeing Neeraj Chopra compete at the Asian Games , describing the Indian star's absence as "bad luck" after an ankle injury forced him out of the continental event.Chopra, a two-time Olympic medallist, was unable to defend the Asian Games men's javelin gold he won in the previous edition in China after suffering an ankle ligament tear during training last month.Pathirage made the most of Chopra's absence, producing a winning throw of 88.55m with his sixth and final attempt to claim gold at the rain-affected Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium on Monday.India's Yashvir Singh, who replaced the injured Chopra in the athletics team, took silver with a personal best of 85.72m, while Rohit Yadav secured bronze with 84.35m."Yeah, he had a little injury on the ankle after Lausanne Diamond League. It's his bad luck," the 23-year-old Pathirage told PTI when asked if he was missing Chopra after the event."I do sometimes speak to him (Chopra)," he added.Pathirage and Chopra have shared the field at major competitions, with the Indian also inviting the Sri Lankan to compete at the inaugural NC Classic javelin competition in Bengaluru in July last year.Chopra won that event with a throw of 86.18m, while Pathirage finished third with 84.34m.The results have been very different this year.Pathirage has won all three competitions in which Chopra competed. He began by winning the Doha Diamond League in June, where Chopra finished fourth. The Sri Lankan then claimed gold at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games, with Chopra taking silver.The pattern continued at the Lausanne Diamond League in August, where Pathirage finished first and Chopra was second.Pathirage has also been in remarkable form throughout the season, recording three throws beyond 90m. He has finished first in 13 of the 14 events he has competed in this year, with a second-place finish in the remaining competition.His list of titles includes four Diamond League meetings, the Diamond League Final, World Athletics Ultimate Championships, Commonwealth Games and now the Asian Games.Despite the dominance, Pathirage insisted there was no elaborate secret behind his success."No secret, just normal training every year," he said when asked about his form and three 90m-plus throws this season.Pathirage also praised the two Indian throwers who shared the podium with him in Chopra's absence."Yashvir and Rohit are very good. His average throw has been 85m. Maybe, I think, next year, Yashvir and Rohit can produce big throws for India."The result completed a South Asian sweep of the men's javelin medals at both the Commonwealth Games and Asian Games.For Pathirage, however, the winning throw fell short of what he had hoped to achieve."The conditions were not good due to rain.""I could not get proper grip of my javelin. I had wanted to break the Games record and Asian record but I could not go for my massive throws like 90m."But I am happy to be the first-ever Sri Lankan javelin throw gold medal winner at the Asian Games."Pathirage has already turned his attention towards his next major targets."My next target is World Championship next year and then 2028 LA Olympics."The Sri Lankan made his World Championships debut last year but believes he will enter the next edition with greater experience."I competed for the first time in the World Championships last year, when I had less experience. Now, I have some experience and let us see what happens. I will give my best."
Article Summary: Sri Lankan javelin thrower Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage won gold at the Asian Games. Pathorage has won all three competitions in which Indian Neeraj Chopra has competed. Pathrage has finished first in 13 of the 14 events he has competed in this year.

Article Title: EXCLUSIVE | 'Olympics sapna hai': Yashvir Singh after ticking off Asian Games and CWG medal boxes
Article Text:
India's Yashvir Singh celebrates winning the silver medal in the men's javelin throw final at the Asian Games. (AP Photo)

Another final throw

'Grip slip ho rahi thi'

Back-to-back major medals
